title: Beyond Heuristics: Learnable Density Control for 3D Gaussian Splatting
claim: Prior methods use handcrafted threshold rules for adaptive control; a learned policy network adapts better and recovers finer detail.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, zoomed red-box crops at right
description: Two horizontally stacked panels separated by a line. Panel (a) FastGS shows initial orange Gaussian ellipses feeding a dashed box titled Heuristic Density Control Paradigm. The box holds a piecewise rule set (clone, split, prune, maintain) with threshold inequalities. An arrow leads to a rendered bonsai-and-bicycle scene, PSNR 30.10. Panel (b) LeGS shows the same initial Gaussians feeding a dashed box titled Learnable Density Control Paradigm. It contains Gaussian Attribution, a Policy Network (neural net icon, π_θ), an Action box (maintain, clone, split, prune with icons), and a reward loop (Render w/o G_i, Compute Reward, Ground Truth Image, update arrow). Output render shows PSNR 33.08. At the far right, red-box zoomed crops of the wheel and Gaussian-ellipse overlays contrast the under-densified result with the denser one. The eye goes first to the equations in (a) and the network in (b).
caption: Comparison between our LeGS and FastGS. The heuristic paradigm, relying on a manually-designed score function with a fixed threshold, achieves suboptimal results. For instance, FastGS tends to under-densify Gaussians in wheel (red box), causing artifacts. In contrast, our learning-based paradigm effectively captures intricate local details.
abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated impressive real-time rendering performance, its efficacy remains constrained by a reliance on heuristic density control. Despite numerous refinements to these handcrafted rules, such methods inherently lack the flexibility to adapt to diverse scenes with complex geometries. In this paper, we propose a paradigm shift for density control from rigid heuristics to fully learnable policies. Specifically, we introduce \textbf{LeGS}, a framework that reformulates density control as a parameterized policy network optimized via Reinforcement Learning (RL). Central to our approach is the tailored effective reward function grounded in sensitivity analysis, which precisely quantifies the marginal contribution of individual Gaussians to reconstruction quality. To maintain computational tractability, we derive a closed-form solution that reduces the complexity of reward calculation from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$. Extensive experiments on the Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks \& Temples, and Deep Blending datasets demonstrate that \textbf{LeGS} significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, striking a superior balance between reconstruction quality and efficiency. The code will be released at https://github.com/AaronNZH/LeGS
